title: Anthropic is reportedly in talks to buy Decart for $6bn, its biggest deal yet
excerpt: Anthropic is reportedly in talks to buy Israeli startup Decart for about $6bn, its largest deal yet, a wager on efficiency rather than scale as it readies an IPO.
content_html:
Anthropic is reportedly in talks to acquire Decart, an Israeli AI startup, for roughly $6bn, according to reports attributed to Reuters.

If it happens, it would be the largest deal in Anthropic’s history. The talks are not final, both companies declined to comment, and the whole thing could still fall apart.

What makes the story worth pausing on is not the price but the target. Decart does not build a rival chatbot. It builds software that squeezes more work out of the same chips, cutting the cost of training and running AI models.

In an era of thrift-maxxing, where cheap Chinese models keep undercutting Western labs and investors have grown wary of bottomless compute bills, that is a pointed thing to spend $6bn on.

Decart was founded in 2023 by three Israeli engineers, Dean Leitersdorf, Orian Leitersdorf, and Moshe Shalev. Alongside its efficiency work, it has a flashier side in generative video and world models, showcased in its Oasis demo back in October 2024.

But it is the unglamorous chip-efficiency layer, the part that quietly lowers the electricity bill, that fits Anthropic’s current preoccupations rather than the eye-catching video tricks.

The price tag reflects a rapid re-rating. Decart was valued at $3.1bn a year ago, in August 2025, then nudged towards $4bn this May after a $300m round led by Radical Ventures.

A $6bn deal would mark a premium of roughly 50% over that most recent mark, which is a brisk climb for a two-year-old company.

Anthropic, for its part, is operating on a different scale entirely. Its own valuation has ballooned to somewhere around $965bn after its most recent mega-round, and in early June it confidentially filed an S-1 with the SEC, the paperwork that precedes a public listing.

This would be its fifth acquisition of the year, following at least four smaller ones, but by far the biggest, and the timing so close to a listing is unlikely to be a coincidence.

The logic is not hard to read. Anthropic is locked in the same compute arms race as everyone else, and the cost of that race is the number every prospective public-market investor will scrutinise most closely.

Buying a company whose entire purpose is to make each chip go further is a way of shoring up the infrastructure and controlling costs before the books go on display.

It is a rare and rather European sort of moment, an AI leader spending big precisely so that it can spend less, and betting that thrift, not sheer size, is what the market now wants to see.

That instinct is already visible elsewhere in Anthropic’s dealmaking. It recently signed a multi-year GPU deal with CoreWeave to run Claude at production scale, part of a wider scramble to lock in capacity on terms it can live with.

An efficiency acquisition would be the other half of the same equation, wringing more from the hardware it is busy securing.

Anthropic was not the only suitor circling, either. Nvidia, SpaceX, and Amazon were all reportedly interested in Decart, which tells you the market has decided efficiency is now a strategic asset in its own right rather than a nice-to-have.

When the chipmaker itself, a rocket company, and a cloud giant are all sniffing around the same startup, the thesis is no longer niche.

There is a tidy irony in all of this. The frontier labs spent years insisting that the path to better AI ran through ever-larger models and ever-larger data centres.

Now, with an IPO in view and a cost-conscious market rewarding thrift, one of the loudest champions of scale is reportedly willing to pay a record sum to get smaller, cheaper, and leaner.

content_html_zh:
据路透社报道，据报道，Anthropic 正在洽谈以约 60 亿美元收购以色列人工智能初创公司 Decart。

如果真的发生，这将是 Anthropic 历史上最大的一笔交易。 谈判尚未最终确定，两家公司都拒绝置评，整个事情仍有可能破裂。

这个故事值得停下来的不是价格，而是目标。 Decart 不会构建竞争对手的聊天机器人。 它构建的软件可以从相同的芯片中挤出更多的工作，从而降低训练和运行人工智能模型的成本。

在一个节俭的时代，廉价的中国模型不断削弱西方实验室的竞争力，投资者对无底的计算费用越来越警惕，在这方面花费 60 亿美元是有针对性的。

Decart 由三位以色列工程师 Dean Leitersdorf、Orian Leitersdorf 和 Moshe Shalev 于 2023 年创立。 除了提高效率之外，它在生成视频和世界模型方面也有更华丽的一面，早在 2024 年 10 月的 Oasis 演示中就展示了这一点。

但真正适合 Anthropic 当前关注点的是不起眼的芯片效率层，即悄悄降低电费的部分，而不是引人注目的视频技巧。

价格标签反映了快速的重新评级。 一年前，即 2025 年 8 月，Decart 的估值为 31 亿美元，今年 5 月，在 Radical Ventures 领投的 3 亿美元融资后，Decart 的估值升至 40 亿美元。

一笔 60 亿美元的交易将比最近的价格溢价约 50%，这对于一家成立两年的公司来说是一个快速的攀升。

就人择而言，其运作规模完全不同。 在最近一轮大型融资后，该公司的估值已飙升至 9650 亿美元左右，并于 6 月初向 SEC 秘密提交了 S-1，这是公开上市之前的文件。

这将是该公司今年的第五次收购，此前至少有四次规模较小的收购，但也是迄今为止规模最大的一次收购，而且时机如此接近上市不太可能是巧合。

逻辑并不难读。 Anthropic 和其他人一样陷入了同样的计算军备竞赛，而这场竞赛的成本是每个潜在的公开市场投资者都会最密切关注的数字。

收购一家公司的全部目的是让每个芯片走得更远，这是在书籍展示之前支撑基础设施和控制成本的一种方式。

这是一个罕见的、颇为欧洲式的时刻，人工智能领导者投入大量资金正是为了减少支出，而市场现在希望看到的是节俭而不是纯粹的规模。

这种本能在 Anthropic 的交易中的其他地方已经可见。 它最近与 CoreWeave 签署了一项多年 GPU 协议，以生产规模运行 Claude，这是更广泛争夺的一部分，旨在按照其可以接受的条件锁定产能。

效率获取将是同一方程式的另一半，从其忙于保护的硬件中榨取更多资源。

人择也不是唯一的追求者。 据报道，Nvidia、SpaceX 和亚马逊都对 Decart 感兴趣，这表明市场已经决定效率本身就是一项战略资产，而不是一种可有可无的资产。

当芯片制造商本身、一家火箭公司和一家云巨头都在关注同一家初创公司时，这个论文就不再是利基市场了。

这一切充满讽刺意味。 前沿实验室多年来坚持认为，通往更好人工智能的道路需要不断扩大的模型和越来越大的数据中心。

现在，考虑到首次公开募股和注重成本的市场奖励节俭，据报道，最响亮的规模拥护者之一愿意支付创纪录的金额来变得更小、更便宜、更精简。
